summary: Otto Karow worked in Sinology, Japanology, and Tibetology. He studied at Giessen, Berlin (~1931–1935), Leipzig, and Bonn (PD 1948–1952). He taught at Bonn (1947), Münster (1951–1957), and Goethe University Frankfurt as professor of East Asian Philology (1960–1978).

Otto Loth worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and other fields. He studied under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer (~1865–1869) and held a post at the University of Leipzig (~1874–1881).

Otto Maenchen-Helfen specialized in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Vienna, Gothenburg, and Leipzig (Ph.D. under August Conrady). He held posts at the Marx-Engels Institute, Berlin, Mills College, and UC Berkeley (1947–1962).

Otto Rosenberg was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology. He studied at Saint Petersburg, Bonn (1909), and under Theodore Stcherbatsky, Sergey Oldenburg, Hermann Jacobi, and Rudolf Lange, later teaching at Saint Petersburg State University (1911–1919).

Otto Schlaginhaufen earned his Ph.D. from the University of Zurich in 1905. He worked at the Rudolf-Virchow-Sammlung (1905–1906), the Museum of Ethnology, Dresden (1906–1911), and the University of Zurich as professor of anthropology (ao. 1911, ord. 1917–1950).

Otto Schrader specialized in linguistics and Indology, studying at Jena, Berlin, and Leipzig (Ph.D. ~1876–1877). He taught at Carolo-Alexandrinum Jena (1877–1909), the University of Jena (ao. Professor 1890), and the University of Breslau (ord. Professor 1909).

Otto Spies worked in religious studies and Indology. He earned a Ph.D. at Tübingen under Enno Littmann and a Dr. juris at Bonn. He served as professor at Aligarh Muslim University (1932–1936), Breslau (1936), and Bonn (1951–1971).

Otto Stein worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at Charles University/German University in Prague under Moriz Winternitz and Heinrich Swoboda, later serving as professor of Indology at Charles University/German University in Prague (1930–1939).

Otto Strauss was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Munich, Berlin, and Kiel (Ph.D. under Hermann Oldenberg). He held academic posts at Kiel University (PD 1911, ao. Professor 1920), the University of Calcutta (1913–1920), and Breslau (1928–1935).
Otto Stursberg worked in the fields of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, completing his PhD between ~1903 and 1907 under the supervision of Richard Pischel.
Otto Walter was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. studies at the University of Strasbourg between ~1900 and 1903 under the supervision of Ernst Leumann.

Otto Wecker worked in Indology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Münster, and the University of Tübingen, where he earned his PhD (~1903–1905) under Richard von Garbe. He later taught at the University of Göttingen (1947–1953).

Indologist and linguist Otto von Böhtlingk studied at Saint Petersburg, Berlin, and Bonn under Franz Bopp, Christian Lassen, and A. W. von Schlegel. He served at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences (director 1849–1868) and the University of Jena (~1868–1885).

Otton Ottonovič Rozenberg worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Saint Petersburg under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy, Bonn under Hermann Jacobi, and Berlin under Rudolf Lange. He became a professor at Saint Petersburg State University in 1919.

Owen Flanagan is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fordham University (~1968–1972) and Boston University (~1972–1977), and he was appointed Professor of Philosophy at Duke University circa 1996.

Owen Lattimore worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Harvard University (1928–1929) and later held a post at the University of Leeds (~1963–1970).

P. A. Payutto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his bachelor's degree at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1956–1962), where he served as Associate Dean (~1964–1972), and was named Tipitaka Acharaya at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1995.

P. Anujan Achan worked in the fields of Indology and history and archaeology. He studied under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya and held the post of Government Archaeologist at the Thrissur Zoo and State Museum.
P. B. Meegaskumbura is an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at the University of Peradeniya, with his post attested in 1991 and 2010.

P. D. Premasiri is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Peradeniya, Cambridge, and Hawaiʻi (PhD under Eliot Deutsch). He spent his primary career at the University of Peradeniya, serving as department head (1997–2004) and professor (attested 2010).
